title: ICMR National Guidelines on Acute Febrile Illness and Antipyretic Safety

chunks.content: Paracetamol (500mg to 650mg in adults with normal renal and hepatic function, every 4 to 6 hours as needed, maximum 4g per 24 hours; pediatric dose strictly weight-based at 10-15 mg/kg per dose) remains the safest foundational first-line antipyretic. In acute viral fevers and monsoon seasonal fevers across northern and eastern India, Aspirin and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as Ibuprofen and Diclofenac must be strictly avoided due to potential risks of hemorrhagic manifestations in endemic Dengue and Reye's syndrome in pediatric cohorts.
chunks.contraindications: Severe active liver disease, chronic heavy alcohol intake, hypersensitivity to paracetamol.
chunks.warnings: Do not exceed maximum daily dosage. Seek urgent hospital triage if fever exceeds 102°F (38.9°C), persists beyond 72 hours, or presents with altered sensorium, stiff neck, or petechial rash.
chunks.home_care: Adequate oral fluid hydration (ORS, coconut water, clean boiled water), resting in a well-ventilated room, and tepid sponging using lukewarm water. Never use ice or cold water for sponging as it induces shivering and elevates core temperature.
chunks.citation: ICMR Acute Febrile Illness Diagnostic and Management Framework (2024), Section 4: Antipyretic Principles, pp. 22-26.
